title: August and the Letters
premise: Marine biologist Rosalind Vasquez returns to the coastal town of August Bay to catalog a dying sea turtle population and to quietly claim the beach house her estranged grandmother left her—along with a box of unsent letters that reveal a hidden family she never knew. Stranded by an early snowstorm with Theo Marchetti, the rival researcher who broke her heart in grad school, and his young daughter Juniper, Rosalind must decide whether the walls she built around her heart are protection or just another kind of cage. As the letters unravel the truth about her grandmother's own lost love, Rosalind risks everything at the town's Festival of Lights, confessing her feelings to Theo and choosing to stay in August Bay—not as an heir to a house, but as founder of the family she never expected.
about_author: Wendell Galloway is the pen name of a former tide-pool docent who spent a decade writing love letters he never mailed. He now lives on a cold coast, where he collects sea glass and believes every storm is a plot device.

chapters.title: The House That Waited
chapters.summary: Rosalind arrives in August Bay to survey nesting sites and claims the keys to her late grandmother's beach house, finding it frozen mid-life—with a locked cedar box of letters addressed to someone named 'A.' POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: guarded grief mixed with curiosity; she plans to sell and leave by spring.

chapters.title: Snow on the Survey Line
chapters.summary: During a coastal survey, Rosalind discovers the competing research grant went to Theo Marchetti—her grad school rival and the man she loved and left. A freak snowstorm strands them both, plus Theo's quiet seven-year-old daughter Juniper, at the beach house. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: dread curdling into reluctant intimacy as the roads close.

chapters.title: Three Plates at Dinner
chapters.summary: Storm-bound, they negotiate fragile truce over canned chowder while Juniper sketches turtles. Rosalind learns Theo's wife left when Juniper was two; Theo learns Rosalind never got the letter he sent after their falling-out. POV: alternating, opening with Theo for the first time. Emotional beat: old wounds reopened gently, first thaw.

chapters.title: Letters to A.
chapters.summary: Rosalind pries open the cedar box and reads her grandmother's decades of unsent letters to a lighthouse keeper named August—the town's namesake—who died before they could marry. POV: Rosalind, interwoven with letter excerpts. Emotional beat: recognition that hiding from love is an inheritance she can refuse.

chapters.title: Juniper's Map
chapters.summary: Roads clear but none of them leave. Juniper enlists Rosalind in a treasure hunt based on the letters, leading them to the decommissioned lighthouse where August's belongings remain. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: Theo watches Rosalind become unguarded with his daughter and realizes he's falling again—and fears repeating history.

chapters.title: The Rival Grant
chapters.summary: Theo's university demands he return early to defend his funding against a bid that would shutter both research programs—including Rosalind's turtle survey. They must collaborate or compete. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: professional stakes entangle with personal ones; a heated argument ends almost in a kiss, interrupted by Juniper.

chapters.title: What the Tide Took
chapters.summary: A cold-stunned sea turtle washes ashore during a second storm; the three rescue it together through the night in the house's converted garage. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: working side by side, hands touching over the same small life, Rosalind admits to herself she wants to stay—but old fear whispers that staying means losing.

chapters.title: The Letter He Sent
chapters.summary: Rosalind finds Theo's decade-old letter, forwarded twice and finally delivered inside her grandmother's forwarded mail—it had been waiting in the cedar box all along. She learns why he pushed her away in grad school: a family crisis he was ashamed of. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: fury dissolving into grief; she realizes she punished him for a silence she also kept.

chapters.title: Festival of Lights
chapters.summary: At the town festival, Rosalind publicly presents the joint research plan saving both programs, then reads one of her grandmother's letters aloud from the lighthouse steps before finding Theo and confessing—choosing him and Juniper with her whole heart, not pieces. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: climax; vulnerability as triumph, the whole town as witness.

chapters.title: August, At Last
chapters.summary: Spring arrives: the rescued turtle is released, the beach house becomes a field station and home, and Rosalind mails her grandmother's final letter to August's surviving niece, closing the circle. Theo and Juniper move in; the three hang a new nameplate. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: resolution—found family, claimed identity, love that stayed.
